cards.front: What should you know about drama exam tips?
cards.back: For the practical exam, the examiner assesses: 1) Vocal skills (clarity, projection, pace, pitch), 2) Physical skills (movement, gesture, facial expression, spatial awareness), 3) Characterisation (understanding, truthfulness, development), 4) Interaction (listening, responding, ensemble awareness), 5) Overall effectiveness (impact, engagement, dramatic shape).

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: If someone in your group forgets their lines or makes a mistake, your mark will be affected too. Correct: You are assessed INDIVIDUALLY. If another performer makes a mistake, the examiner watches how YOU respond — staying in character, adapting and supporting the scene shows professionalism and can actually enhance your mark. Component 3 (Texts in Practice, 30%) is assessed by a visiting examiner on AO3 (perform with understanding). The two extracts must come from the same play. The examiner assesses each performer individually on vocal skills, physical skills, characterisation, interaction and overall effectiveness. Maximum marks require exceptional commitment, truthfulness and dramatic impact.
